display.what_is_stored: display-referred colour, not radiance: the exposure and the display curve have already been applied, and the table is inside 0..1.  The runtime applies the sRGB transfer function once at output and must not tone map, expose or gamma-encode again.
display.colour_space: linear sRGB, IEC 61966-2-1 primaries, D65 white
display.adaptation: middle-grey auto exposure, one scalar per sun step: the mean luminance of the visible hemisphere is put on adapted_level (0.36) by solving the curve for the exposure, E = -ln(1 - L) / mean.  That is what an engine does with a frame histogram; the "frame" here is the sky of that sun step, which is why noon and sunset can share one screen.  The mean, not the median: the median ignores the sunward quadrant, which is the light a low sun puts you in.  Only scattered sunlight is metered, and the gain is capped at adaptation_gain_max, because adaptation has a floor and a sky that is nothing but airglow must not be lifted into daylight
display.airglow_is_post_exposure: the night airglow is an emission and a display calibration, so it is added after the step's exposure and is never metered: a night therefore stays dark instead of being scaled up by the adaptation of an almost-black sky
display.tone_curve: C = 1 - exp(-L * exposure), applied per channel, which is the display equation of both reference implementations of this model (Bruneton's 2017 demo, Hillaire's 2020 demo) and nothing else.  It is linear for small L, so the sky's measured colour reaches the screen; it never reaches 1, so nothing is pinned at white; and each channel rolls off on its own, so a bright warm highlight desaturates toward white the way a camera's does instead of rotating to yellow or saturating to red
display.transfer_function: IEC 61966-2-1 sRGB OETF, applied at the output boundary: C' = 12.92 C below 0.0031308, else 1.055 C^(1/2.4) - 0.055.  This is not pow(C, 1/2.2).
display.no_extra_steps: there is no fitted film curve, no chroma multiplier, no gamut fit and no clamp after the curve: earlier bakes carried an ACES-on-luminance step, a sky_saturation (1.5) chroma scale, a per-channel clamp with a highlight desaturation ramp and a percentile glare limit, and each of them was compensating for the previous one.  All four are gone; --verify measures what is left (mid-tone colour preservation and the display range)

dome.altitude_mapping: row = (sin(altitude) + 1) / 2 * (altitude_samples - 1); row 0 = nadir, the middle row straddles the horizon, last row = zenith
dome.azimuth_mapping: u = atan2(dir.z, dir.x) / 2pi, 0 at +x, increasing toward +z
dome.solid_angle: rows uniform in sin(altitude) -> equal solid angle per row/column

physics.model: single-scattering Rayleigh atmosphere with aerosol Mie scattering
physics.spectrum_to_xyz: band radiances are reconstructed as a piecewise-linear spectrum in wavelength and integrated against the CIE 1931 2-degree observer, then converted to linear sRGB (D65)
physics.note: Direct solar disk is not baked in; the renderer draws it separately.  The table holds display colour (see display); stats.max_radiance is the pre-display peak.

integration.minecraft_celestial_angle: our sun angle == dayTime / 24000 * 360 (0 = sunrise at 06:00, 90 = noon, 180 = sunset, 270 = midnight)
integration.sun_geometry: the drawn sun is vanilla's sprite on a quad of SUN_QUAD = 7.5 units at distance 100 (8.6 degrees across, white core 2.15 degrees).  The light source baked here is the real disc (sun_disk.angular_diameter_degrees, 0.53), and sun_disk.colour / sun_disk.luminance are how the renderer paints that sprite: alpha-blended with the measured beam colour, dimmed by the beam's own luminance.  It used to be added at full white on top of the baked aureole, which saturates the whole sprite wherever the sky is already near white.
integration.sun_tint: the sprite's colour is sun_disk.colour[step] (the transmitted sunlight, brightest channel 1), scaled by sun_disk.luminance[step]^0.5 and drawn alpha-blended, so where the sprite is bright it replaces the sky instead of adding to it.  sun_disk_tint[step] is the old hue-only relative tint (brightest channel 1, dims towards sunset); it is kept for viewers that draw a flat square rather than the vanilla texture.
integration.sun_elevations: sun_elevation_degrees is the elevation of the centre of the disc, which is also where the renderer draws it; sun_visible_fraction is the part of the disc above the observer's horizon.  Step = celestial angle: 0 sunrise, 90 noon, 180 sunset.
integration.sky_lookup: world direction -> v = (dir.y + 1) / 2 (0 nadir, 0.5 horizon, 1 zenith), u = atan2(dir.z, dir.x) / 2pi (0 at +x, increasing toward +z)
integration.gpu_streaming: two tables (current + next) and a blend factor are enough; nothing else has to be resident

ground.albedo_model: Lambertian surface albedo in the transport: the ground re-emits albedo/pi * (direct sun + sky irradiance) and that light is scattered once toward the eye along the view ray (Rayleigh phase integrated over the lower hemisphere, Mie likewise with its own backscatter fraction).  First order: the bounce does not re-illuminate the ground.  Not applied to the overcast variants.
ground.description: rows below the horizon hold the sky at the mirrored altitude (same azimuth), scaled by 1 - (1 - dim) * smoothstep(0, fade_depth_sin, |sin(altitude)|); the scale is exactly 1 at the horizon so the two halves join without a seam

multiple_scattering.model: successive orders with an isotropic source from order 2 on

cloud.model: none: cloud-free single + multiple scattering bake

airglow.limb_brightening: van Rhijn V(z) = [1 - (R/(R+h))^2 sin^2 z]^-1/2 for a 90 km emitting shell, capped at 80 degrees zenith angle where the real brightness peaks and the geometric factor would diverge
airglow.colour: the three lines through the CIE 1931 observer are a photopic green (0.804, 1.147, 0.120); at airglow levels vision is rod-based, so the colour that arrives at the eye is pulled 75 % toward a blue-shifted neutral of the same luminance (Purkinje shift, rod peak 500 nm).  A dark-adapted observer sees a faint blue-grey, not the green a long exposure records
airglow.calibration: the zenith level is a display calibration of 2.5e-3 scene luminance, chosen so the baked night sky stays visible at the daylight exposure; a physical 21.9 mag/arcsec^2 sky (~1.7e-4 cd/m^2) would be invisible.  It is added after the exposure, so it is not amplified at night.  The spectrum, the scotopic colour and the angular distribution are physical, the level is not.
airglow.weather: clear table only: overcast hides it, so the rain/thunder blend removes it

moon.model: the full moon is the anti-solar light source: the sky it lights is row (sun step + 180) % 360 of this same table, with no extra bake and no phase term
moon.gain: the renderer multiplies the anti-solar *display* colour by a display gain (0.06), not by the physical ratio: 1/398000 of the daylight sky is below one code value at a fixed daylight exposure, so the night level is a calibration like the airglow's, while the angular distribution and the colour are physical
moon.limits: full moon only, and sky only: no phase term, no earthshine on the moon, no terrain lighting beyond the fog colour the renderer already takes from the dome

aerosol.daily_cycle: the Mie coefficient is multiplied by 1 - gain * cos(celestial angle): 1 - gain at sunrise, 1 at noon, 1 + gain at sunset.  The scaled Mie term enters the transmittance, the multiple-scattering solve and the sun-path extinction, so dusk really is hazier, not just tinted.  cos() is continuous over the 360 -> 0 wrap, so there is no seam at dawn.
aerosol.aureole: above 4 degrees of solar elevation the aerosol forward lobe is clipped to the phase it already has 45 degrees from the sun, so the sunward sky keeps the shorter-path gradient but not the peak; the clip ramps in fully by 20 degrees of solar elevation, and at and below 4 degrees (sunset, sunrise) the tabulated phase is untouched.  The peak is real single scattering, but with a hemisphere-metered exposure and no observer glare it rendered as a white disc around the sun.  --aureole 0 disables the clip.
aerosol.limits: the Mie multiplier is haze, not rain: it reddens and dims the light on its way to the cloud deck.  The rain and thunder variants get their grey from the deck (see cloud).

sun_disk.occlusion: resolved per scattering point by the transmittance lookup, so the high atmosphere stays lit after the disc has set
sun_disk.tint: area-weighted mean transmittance of the part of the disc still visible to the observer, held at its sunset value once the whole disc is down so the drawn quad never fades to black
sun_disk.colour_space: linear sRGB, brightest channel 1: the transmitted sunlight this bake computes. Reference for the shape: SKYSPECTRA's direct-normal spectra (Zenodo 8147546), 2 083 measured spectra at 420-780 nm with the Sun 12-70 degrees up, whose chromaticity moves from (0.376, 0.386) at 50-70 degrees to (0.420, 0.414) at 12-16; this bake gives (0.343, 0.353) and (0.380, 0.385).  The field this replaces, sun_disk_tint_bright, normalised the tint by its own luminance and clamped, which turned the 10-degree beam from (1.00, 0.63, 0.25) into (1.00, 0.97, 0.49): a white sun over a gold aureole, which is what reads as 'the sun is way too bright just above the horizon'.
sun_disk.luminance_definition: photopic luminance of the transmitted beam relative to the noonday beam, so 1 at the top of the arc.  SKYSPECTRA's measured direct-normal irradiance gives 0.55 of the 50-70 degree value at 12-16 degrees of elevation; this bake's transmittance gives 0.71 at 15 degrees, the difference being the measured site's aerosol load.
sun_disk.drawing: the renderer paints vanilla's sun sprite with colour * luminance^0.5, alpha-blended (the sprite's own brightness is its alpha), so the disc carries the measured hue and dims with the beam instead of adding a clipped white square on top of its aureole.  The exponent is a display choice for a sprite that is 4x the real disc across: without it the sprite is at full brightness at every elevation, which is the reported "sun is way too bright just above the horizon".
